# /crav1-tasks-ready-to-build

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Tasks ready to build](../../from-tasks-ready-to-build.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

List the tasks ready to build, for one spec or all, and why the others are blocked. Rewrites each slice build map.

**[`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md)** reads `spec.md` open questions, `plan.md` (the `Reviewed:` line and `## Risks`), `tasks.md`, and `verify.md` for one slice or every slice. A ticked task is Done when `verify.md` lists it as verified, otherwise Needs verify. Then a task is blocked by a missing `plan.md`, by a kept-open question whose `Blocks:` line names it, by a kept-open question with no `Blocks:` line (tasks named in the text, or the whole slice only when none are named and resolve-open-questions has never been recorded), by a plan Risk that says do not implement until resolved only when that question has no `Blocks:` line, or by an unticked task in its `(after: T#)` (recorded) or, with no `(after: …)`, the task just before it (inferred). `Blocks: none` blocks no task. Any `Blocks:` line wins over that Risk wording. Lists and Next follow dependency order (1.103.0): the `(after: …)` graph in waves, lowest number first in a wave; Next is the ready task that unblocks the most; a cycle blocks its tasks. It may run `scripts/task_order.py` and `scripts/question_blocks.py` next to the skill. Otherwise it is Ready, with a warning when the plan review is unknown (inferred) or still has open `P#`s.

Shows summary counts per slice, then Ready and Held grouped by build-map branch, Waits in order, and Blocked (one reason each, recorded or inferred), Needs verify, a Done count, one `Next:` line per ready branch, and a `Source:` line. A wait on a real earlier task is Waits in order. A cycle, or an after: that names no task, is Blocked. An open question is Held with that question. Local only: it never reads Azure Boards and names [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md) for task states there. It runs no other skill. It can run any time. It is cross-cutting. It is not a starter option.

1.141.0: an unapproved `## Approval needed` item holds its `Holds:` tasks. They are Waiting on that person. Other tasks still start (`ready-partial`). A matching `Approved:` line clears the hold. `task_order.py` lists them under Waiting on approval.

1.64.0: shows a task's `(branch: …)` and one Branches line from local git only.

1.68.0: the `Sub-branches:` and `left behind:` lines and `merged, reverted on <base> (<sha>)`, report only.

1.69.0: the `Promotion:` line under the Branches line, with the optional `pipeline runs` check.

1.88.0: command-only (`disable-model-invocation: true`). It runs only when you type [`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md); the agent does not start it from a plain question, and its description no longer loads in every chat.

1.125.0: `Blocks: none` blocks no task. A `Blocks:` line wins over a Risk that says do not implement until resolved. No line still blocks the whole slice. Older specs with no line behave as before.

1.126.0: a Risk that says do not implement until resolved matches a question on the question first sentence, a `(question: <first words>)` tag, or the same Blocks tasks named in the Risk. A Risk that matches no question still blocks the slice. `scripts/task_order.py --json` uses T1 style ids.

1.127.0: the report splits Ready, Waiting on a question, Waits in order, and Blocked. `task_order.py` text uses the same Waits in order and Blocked headings. Who on a question comes from "Waiting for", then the latest Pending or Asked line, or not named yet. The interpreter is `docs/reference/running-scripts.md`.

1.128.0: every run rewrites `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md` through `scripts/build_map.py`. The task list is unchanged apart from one line pointing at that file. The word `build-map` shows only the short summary: the path, how many branches in each wave can run in parallel, then the Overlap lines for that wave, one per pair. The ready-check list stays the one pointer line. One branch per numbered Approach step, unless a task has `(map:)`. `(step:)` links a task to a step. No steps, or steps that name no task, means one branch per task, and the file says so. Each wave is a subgraph so its branches sit side by side. A question hold is counted in the wave heading (`3 branches, 2 can start now`). An overlap note names two branches in one wave that share a `(spec:)` requirement or a backtick path. The note does not change readiness or waves. Six fields per branch, no task ids and no file list in a row. Who uses the 1.127.0 rule. A cycle or an unknown `(after:)` is under Blocked.

1.129.0: the row branch is `(map:)`, else `(branch:)`, else the plan step, else `committed later on`, else `feat/<slug>-<words>`. `--recommend T#` prints that name and does not write. Tasks are short names (a `task: T#` title in `work-item.md`, else the text up to ` (`, `, in `, or the sentence end, about 80 characters). A removed task id does not leave a dangling possessive, empty parentheses, a leading comma, or a double space. The wave heading is always `N branches, M can start now`, including `1 branch, 1 can start now`. A row whose task text names another branch adds `Task text names feat/x; built on feat/y`.

1.140.0: a branch named on the task line wins over the plan step. That is `(map:)`, else `(branch:)`, else a `feat/…` name in the sentence, else `committed later on`. The plan step is the fallback when the task line names none. `from <base>` after the branch is its base. Two tasks on one step keep their own branches. When the row is that task-line branch, the note is `Plan step names feat/orders-one-commit-cleanup-main; built on feat/orders-host-setup-scripts`. A `(map:)` row that is not the branch in the task text still says `Task text names feat/x; built on feat/y`. `--recommend` does not write. The first line is the branch. Later lines are `source: task line`, `source: build map`, or `source: new`, `from:` when the task line states a base, and `because:` when a merged or deleted branch was skipped. Merged means a recorded merged pull request, or a tip already in the base or the default branch. A branch deleted locally and on the remote is not offered. A name that does not exist yet is offered so it can be created. Local git only. No fetch. CRLF and LF are the same text. A task whose own line records the merge stays on that branch in the map. `--recommend` does not print that branch, including for that task.

1.132.0: the result is `ready`, `ready-partial`, or `not-ready`. `ready-partial` lists the tasks that can start and where the hold begins. A task that waits on a held task is held too, reason `held, waits on T3`. `not-ready` is when nothing can start. A ticked task stays in the build map, struck through with its pull request, branch, or commit. A wave whose every task is done is a details block. The rows stay. The heading counts done tasks apart from branches that can start.

1.133.0: ready tasks and held tasks are grouped by the build-map row. The branch is `scripts/build_map.py --recommend T#`, so it matches the map. Order is wave, then map order. One `Next:` line per ready branch. A held line names the open question and who has it, or `held, waits on T3`. The Tasks field is `T#` plus the short name, and a done task is `~~T# short name~~ ✓ done` with its pull request. The ready-check report uses that same form. The map is rewritten every ready check, so the ids do not go stale. Prose outside the Tasks field still drops a task id, and the dangling-text cleanup stays. The walk record stays `Result: ready-partial`.

1.143.0: `next_lines` recommend [`/crav1-build-walk`](crav1-build-walk.md), with the T number beside the short name and the branch, and name [`/crav1-build-tasks`](crav1-build-tasks.md) for one task without the walk. One line per ready branch. A not-ready result does not print that line.

1.135.0: the ready check compares `tasks.md` with `verify.md`. A ticked task, or a task whose pull request is recorded merged (`(PR n)` and the word merged on the task line or its Match `Branch:` line), that `verify.md` still lists as not implemented, is behind. So is a `Next:` line in `verify.md` that names such a task. The check prints `Waiting: [`/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`](crav1-verify-build-against-spec.md) <slug> - verify.md is behind tasks.md (T2, T45)` and does not print that Next line. It does not write `verify.md`. `build-map.md` stays the one file this command writes.

1.136.0: a `Next:` line is stale only when it names a ticked task. A ticked task still listed as `Not implemented` is behind, and so is a merged task still listed as `Not implemented`. A merged `[ ]` row whose status is `Implemented, verified, tick pending` is not behind. A verify-only change does not force `not-ready`. This command does not restamp `walk-progress.md`. Only the walk's record or `clear --yes` does. `scripts/task_order.py` lists a recorded-merged task under Needs tick. `scripts/resolve_spec.py` resolves a named spec: exact folder first, then one unique playbook basename, spec title, or work-item name. Several matches are listed and the run stops.

1.137.0: a question with no `Blocks:` line holds `T#` ids named in its text that exist in `tasks.md`, shown like a Blocks hold and noted inferred from the text. It holds the whole slice only when no task is named and resolve-open-questions has never been recorded. `Blocks: whole slice` (also `the whole slice`, any case) is a recorded hold of every unfinished task and stays Waiting through spec drift. A question with a `Blocks:` line, or one already recorded as waiting, stays Waiting through spec drift. A new or unparsed question jumps back only for the tasks it holds. `scripts/resolve_spec.py` also accepts one unique ordered token subsequence (`cc 1.0` matches `cc-process-1-0`). No match lists the nearest slugs.

1.144.0: a named spec is `<interpreter> -X utf8 scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs`. On Windows `<interpreter>` is `python` with `PYTHONUTF8=1`. Elsewhere it is `python3`. `--recommend` is `scripts/build_map.py docs/specs/<slug> --recommend T#`. The rule is `docs/reference/running-scripts.md`.

## Choice words

Exact words for bots and scripted runs (no `--flags`). A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words.

| Question | Word | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show the build map? | `build-map` | show only the build map for the same scope, such as cc 1.0; the task list stays off |
| Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` | check the latest successful Azure DevOps runs behind the Promotion line (read-only) |

## Runs when

You want to know which tasks can be built now, and why the others cannot, or you want the build map. Called by the user with its slash command, any time (command-only).

## Prompts

Prompt budget: 0 (asks nothing). A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: `spec.md` open questions, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `verify.md` per slice.

Reads, for one slice or every slice under `docs/specs/`, the open questions in `spec.md` with their `Blocks:`, `Asked:`, `Pending:`, and `Answered:` lines, the `Reviewed:` line, `## Approach`, and `## Risks` in `plan.md`, the task lines in `tasks.md` with their ticks, `(after: T#)`, `(branch:)`, `(step:)`, and `(map:)`, a `task: T#` title in `work-item.md` when that file exists, and `verify.md` when it exists.

## Writes

In short: `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md` every run, with `T#` plus the short name in the Tasks field, and a list in chat grouped by branch.

Writes a list in the chat with summary counts, Ready and Held grouped by build-map branch, Waits in order, Blocked, Needs verify, a Done count, one Next line per ready branch, and its source, plus one line pointing at the build map. Every run rewrites `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md`. The Tasks field is `T#` plus the short name. The word `build-map` prints only the short summary of that file.

## Does not

Leaves every file other than `build-map.md` alone, including `verify.md`, and never reads Azure Boards. It does not commit the map.

Limits and exceptions: does not guess a dependency or a blocking link from task text. Where nothing is recorded it uses a fallback and marks the reason inferred. It writes no readiness marks; review-plan, tighten-plan, plan-from-spec, and resolve-open-questions write them. The map is written only by `scripts/build_map.py`.
